patient.name: Mark D.
patient.weightNote: V1: weight is narrative-only; the engine runs 80 kg adult physiology for every patient.

dispatch.cadText: Caller at picnic says man stung by bee, face puffing up, trouble breathing. Caller thinks he might have fainted but still talking. Says maybe ate peanuts too, not sure. Crowd gathering.
updates: Crowd getting loud, PD en route

scene.description: Morning park picnic area, clear sky, tables and food out, uneven grass, truck parked far on path.

backstory: Anxious and restless, talks fast between breaths and keeps swatting at the air. Scared he will stop breathing and keeps asking if he is going to be okay. Gets frustrated when asked to sit still.
conditionsNote: Dispatch Engine v1: generatorReady conditions only; see skeleton.

bystander.label: Hostile crowd
bystander.notes: Films everything, shouts advice, closes in. One loud voice leads; the rest follow. PD is coming but not here.

persona: Anxious and restless, talks fast between breaths and keeps swatting at the air. Scared he will stop breathing and keeps asking if he is going to be okay. Gets frustrated when asked to sit still.

SAMPLE.signs_symptoms: Swelling at sting on forearm with itching and tight throat and trouble breathing
SAMPLE.allergies: Bee stings cause swelling before, never this bad
SAMPLE.medications: Takes nothing daily, no home meds
SAMPLE.past_history: No ongoing illness, prior local reaction to insect sting
SAMPLE.last_meal: Picnic snacks this morning before sting
SAMPLE.events: Stung while eating outdoors at picnic, swelling started after

OPQRST.onset: Sudden after sting at picnic a short time ago
OPQRST.provokes: Swallowing and deep breaths feel worse, sitting still helps a little
OPQRST.quality: Itchy sting site with tight scratchy throat and chest tightness
OPQRST.radiates: Swelling spreading up arm, tightness in throat and chest
OPQRST.severity_words: Scary and getting worse, throat feels like closing, fear taking over
OPQRST.time: Started minutes after sting and has worsened since

secrets.fact: Has epi pen in bag nearby but has not used it, afraid of needles
secrets.revealWhen: Ask about epi pen or allergy kit or bag

bystanderLines: We got you on video, do something right now, he cant breathe.
Back off, I know first aid, give him water and let him walk it off.
expectedPathway: Scene safety with distance from truck and uneven ground, manage hostile crowd and request PD. Primary assessment for airway and breathing, allergy with anaphylaxis signs. Ask about epi pen use, assist per protocol, oxygen, rapid transport, monitor airway, reassess, calm fearful patient.
